harness: Windsurf / Cascade (IDE + CLI) — the Codeium "Cascade" agent, now shipped as Devin Desktop
vendor: Codeium / Windsurf (Cognition) — product vendor is Windsurf (Codeium); parent is Cognition (Devin)
repo: No public source repo for the Cascade backend. Closest upstream: https://github.com/Exafunction/codeium (archived 2026-10-13, contains the open Codeium extension/language-server protocol) and the public VS Code plugin https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Codeium.codeium (v1.49.2, "Windsurf Plugin (formerly Codeium)"). The shipped plugin bundle was downloaded and inspected for the protobuf descriptors.
surfaces: Windsurf IDE (VS Code fork) Cascade panel; Devin Desktop (Cognition) — same Cascade store, same `.codeium/windsurf` root; Cascade CLI / "Windsurf CLI" (terminal front-end; drives the IDE/language server, no separate session store of its own — no local session log found); VS Code plugin `Codeium.codeium` (Windsurf Plugin) — chat/autocomplete, uses the same `codeium.windsurf` extension globalState but the public build contains no Cascade trajectory/transcript writer.
binaries: Windsurf IDE (VS Code fork) and Devin Desktop; bundled Codeium language server `language_server_windows_x64.exe` at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<Devin|Windsurf>\resources\app\extensions\windsurf\bin\` (runs with `--ide_name windsurf --codeium_dir <dir> --database_dir <dir>`); VS Code plugin `Codeium.codeium` v1.49.2 from the marketplace; optional `wsc` CLI (https://github.com/staronelabs/windsurf-cli) that drives Cascade over the IDE extension (macOS only).

paths: %USERPROFILE%\.windsurf\transcripts\{trajectory_id}.jsonl — native Cascade transcript, JSONL, one file per conversation; lazily materialized (only appears once the `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook is registered); override with env WINDSURF_TRANSCRIPTS_DIR
%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\cascade\{cascade_id}.pb — the always-on conversation store; one AES-256-GCM sealed CortexTrajectory protobuf per conversation
%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\brain\ — plans and other Cascade state (not read by other adapters)
%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\hooks.json — user-level Cascade hook config (Cascade merges system + user + workspace)

%APPDATA%\Windsurf\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb — VS Code-fork global storage; ItemTable key `codeium.windsurf` -> JSON -> `windsurf.state.cachedActiveTrajectory:{ws_id}` -> base64 plaintext protobuf (one working reader; contradicted by a newer upstream check)
%APPDATA%\Windsurf - Next\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb — preview channel variant of the above
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<Devin|Windsurf>\resources\app\extensions\windsurf\bin\language_server_windows_x64.exe — the only tool that can decrypt the .pb store (GetCascadeTrajectory RPC)
storage.format: Three distinct local stores: (1) NATIVE TRANSCRIPT = newline-delimited JSON, one JSON object per step, plaintext; (2) CONVERSATION CACHE = one file per conversation, AES-256-GCM sealed protobuf (CortexTrajectory); (3) legacy VS Code SQLite state.vscdb. There is no always-on plaintext JSONL.
storage.append_semantics: MIXED — this is the blocker for the existing tailer. (1) The native transcript is APPEND-ONLY, LINE-DELIMITED JSONL and is read incrementally by byte offset upstream (ai-guardian `_scan_jsonl_incremental`), so Discodex's existing LogTailer can tail it — BUT it is CUMULATIVE per trajectory (rewritten/grown as steps arrive) and the directory is capped at 100 files, pruned oldest-by-mtime. It also does not exist at all until the `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook is registered. (2) The `.pb` conversation store is a WHOLE-FILE REWRITE, not append-only: each conversation is one sealed blob replaced as steps arrive (upstream caches decryption verdicts by size+mtime, proving mutation), and only the active trajectory is mirrored locally. (3) state.vscdb rows are replaced wholesale and VS Code flushes the DB on a ~60 s idle interval (`AbstractStorageService.DEFAULT_FLUSH_INTERVAL = 60 * 1000` in microsoft/vscode src/vs/platform/storage/common/storage.ts), so even that route lags by up to a minute. (4) The official Cascade HOOK payload is the only strictly ordered, per-tool-step, timestamped live signal: hooks fire synchronously per action (pre/post read_code, write_code, run_command, mcp_tool_use, user_prompt, cascade_response).
storage.session_file_naming: Transcript: `{trajectory_id}.jsonl` under the transcripts dir. Conversation store: `{cascade_id}.pb` under `.codeium/windsurf/cascade/`, and the filename stem IS the session id (upstream: "The session id is `cascade_id`, which is also the file name"). Project grouping: from the trajectory metadata's first workspace entry — `workspace_folder_absolute_uri` and `git_root_absolute_uri` are `file://` URIs; the git root names the project better than the opened folder.

fields.project: RECOVERABLE. Transcript path: not in the line, but the Cascade hook runs with CWD = workspace root (docs: `working_directory` "Defaults to your workspace root"), so the hook can emit the workspace root. Trajectory store: `CortexTrajectoryMetadata.f1 workspaces[].f1 workspace_folder_absolute_uri` / `f2 git_root_absolute_uri` (file:// URIs). state.vscdb route: `User/workspaceStorage/{ws_id}/workspace.json` -> `folder`.
fields.model: RECOVERABLE from the hook payload's common field `model_name` (human-readable, e.g. "Claude Sonnet 4.5", or "Unknown"). In the trajectory protobuf: `CortexStepMetadata.f13 requested_model` (ModelOrAlias) and `f11 generator_model` (enum). NOT present in native transcript lines.
fields.file_basename: RECOVERABLE. Hook payload `tool_info.file_path` for pre/post_read_code and pre/post_write_code. Transcript: the payload dict of the step (e.g. `code_action.path`, `view_file`/`write_to_file` path field) — exact payload key names for tool steps are NOT verified (see risks). Full path must be reduced to basename before publishing.
fields.tool_activity: RECOVERABLE and rich. Hook `agent_action_name` gives the coarse kind (pre/post_read_code, pre/post_write_code, pre/post_run_command, pre/post_mcp_tool_use, pre_user_prompt, post_cascade_response, post_cascade_response_with_transcript, post_setup_worktree). Transcript step `type` values observed in a real 2,093-line trajectory: planner_response (747), run_command (727), code_action (173), user_input (157), view_file (150), mcp_tool (65), list_directory (24), grep_search / grep_search_v2 (13+10, payload key stays `grep_search`), todo_list, find, read_url_content, search_web, view_content_chunk.
fields.phase: RECOVERABLE. pre_* vs post_* distinguishes intent vs completion; transcript line `status` domain observed: done 2047 / canceled 15 / error 31. `post_cascade_response` = turn finished.
fields.timestamps: Hook payload: `timestamp` (ISO 8601) on EVERY event, plus `trajectory_id` and `execution_id` (per-turn id) — this is the only per-tool-step clock and the only source of a task-start instant (pre_user_prompt) and elapsed timer. Trajectory protobuf: `google.protobuf.Timestamp` {f1 seconds, f2 nanos} in `CortexStepMetadata.f1 created_at`, `f7 finished_generating_at`, `f8 completed_at`. Native transcript lines: NO top-level timestamp (verified on a real trajectory: exactly three keys per line, `type`/`status`/payload).

parser_strategy:
TWO OPTIONAL ROUTES; the hook route is the only one that reaches Codex/DSH richness.

ROUTE A (recommended, needs one-time opt-in): Discodex registers an official Cascade hook in `%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\hooks.json` that invokes `discodex cascade-hook`. The hook receives one JSON object on stdin (official schema) and writes ONE sanitized JSON line to a Discodex-owned append-only file. The Rust side then uses the EXISTING LogTailer unchanged. Mapping in `parse_line_for(Provider::Windsurf, line)` over the sanitized line:
- `agent_action_name == "pre_user_prompt"` -> ParsedEvent::TaskStarted { started_at_ms: parse_iso8601(timestamp) } (timer origin)
- every line -> ParsedEvent::AgentDetected { agent: sanitize_model(model_name) } (drop "Unknown", allow-list [A-Za-z0-9 ._-], cap 40 chars)
- `pre_read_code` -> TrackedToolStarted { call_id: execution_id, activity: {label:"Reading project files", file: basename(tool_info.file_path), language: language_from_file(basename)} }; `post_read_code` -> TrackedToolFinished { call_id }
- `pre_write_code` -> TrackedToolStarted { label:"Editing files", file: basename(file_path) }; `post_write_code` -> TrackedToolFinished
- `pre_run_command` -> TrackedToolStarted { label: classify_tool("run_command", tool_info.command_line), file: None }; `post_run_command` -> TrackedToolFinished. The raw command_line is used ONLY to pick a fixed label and is discarded; it is never published.
- `pre_mcp_tool_use` -> TrackedToolStarted { label: "Using MCP tool" or classify_tool(mcp_tool_name), file: basename from mcp_tool_arguments path keys only }; `post_mcp_tool_use` -> TrackedToolFinished. mcp_tool_arguments and mcp_result are never published.
- `post_cascade_response` -> ParsedEvent::Completed (the `response` markdown is discarded)
- `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` -> ParsedEvent::Completed + trigger a transcript re-read
- hook-process CWD (= workspace root) -> ParsedEvent::SessionMetadata { project: basename(cwd), cwd }

ROUTE B (read-only, no config change): tail `%USERPROFILE%\.windsurf\transcripts\{trajectory_id}.jsonl` with the existing LogTailer. `parse_line_for` on `{type, status, <payload>}`: `user_input` -> TaskStarted (timestamp unknown -> use file mtime or fall back to now); `planner_response` -> Thinking/TerminalCandidate; tool types (`view_file`, `write_to_file`, `code_action`, `list_directory`, `run_command`, `grep_search`, `find`, `mcp_tool`, `todo_list`, ...) -> ToolStarted with the basename from the payload's path field. IMPORTANT: derive the payload key as the single key that is neither "type" nor "status" — never derive it from the `type` value (grep_search_v2 keeps payload key `grep_search`). Caveat: this file only exists if the user already registered the transcript hook, and the lines carry no timestamps or model, so the elapsed timer and model are NOT available on this route.

ROUTE C (not recommended): decrypt `.codeium/windsurf/cascade/*.pb` (AES-256-GCM, key `safeCodeiumworldKeYsecretBalloon`) with the `aes-gcm` crate, hand-decode the CortexTrajectory protobuf (field numbers above), and diff whole-file snapshots by step index. Needs a new dependency, a hand-rolled protobuf decoder, a snapshot-diff watcher instead of the tailer, and tolerates only the active trajectory.

FORMAT-CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE:
- The native transcript schema is explicitly unstable: the official docs warn "the exact structure of each step may change in future versions, so please build any hook consumers to be resilient", and the payload key is not always the `type` value (grep_search_v2 keeps payload key `grep_search`). Fail-safe: derive the payload key as "the single key that is not type/status"; ignore unknown types; never derive a payload key from `type`.
- The trajectory protobuf schema also drifts: one upstream reader documents `CortexTrajectory` field 10 `renamed_title`, while the shipped extension descriptor for `CortexTrajectory` has only fields 1-8. Fail-safe: skip unknown field numbers by wire type (both upstream readers do this) and treat a file that decodes but does not match as unreadable.
- The AES-256-GCM key is a hardcoded constant in the language server; it can change. Fail-safe: on GCM authentication failure, skip the file whole and count it; never publish partial or unauthenticated data.
- The hook contract fields (`agent_action_name`, `trajectory_id`, `execution_id`, `timestamp`, `model_name`, `tool_info`) are documented and stable — prefer them over transcript internals for presence/timer/model signals so that transcript churn degrades quality instead of breaking the adapter.
- Never publish: `tool_info.user_prompt`, `tool_info.response`, `tool_info.mcp_result`, `tool_info.mcp_tool_arguments`, `tool_info.edits[].old_string/new_string`, the raw `command_line`, the full `file_path`, and any absolute path. Only basenames, fixed labels, the model name, the phase and the timestamps leave the machine.

risks: NO ALWAYS-ON PLAINTEXT LOG. The native JSONL transcript materializes only once the `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook is registered (upstream: the directory "was absent because it materializes lazily; the directory was conditional"). Without a hook, Discodex sees no local activity log at all, so the feature is opt-in by nature.

THE CONVERSATION STORE IS ENCRYPTED AT REST. `.codeium/windsurf/cascade/*.pb` is AES-256-GCM sealed with a key embedded as a constant in the language server. It is obfuscation, not security, but a Rust adapter needs the `aes-gcm` crate plus a hand-rolled protobuf decoder, and the key/schema can change without notice.

THE .pb STORE IS WHOLE-FILE-REWRITTEN, NOT APPEND-ONLY, and only mirrors the ACTIVE trajectory. Discodex's LogTailer cannot be used on it; a snapshot-diff reader is required, and older conversations are simply not available locally.

CONFLICTING EVIDENCE ON state.vscdb. One upstream reader extracts a plaintext `cachedActiveTrajectory` protobuf from `%APPDATA%\Windsurf\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb`; another, checking Devin Desktop 3.5.17, states "The state.vscdb databases hold no Cascade transcripts on 3.5.17", and a third lists "probe --scan-vscdb — locate Cascade conversations in Windsurf sqlite state" as still being work. Treat the state.vscdb route as UNVERIFIED across current builds; do not ship it as the primary source.
READING state.vscdb NEEDS A NEW SQLITE DEPENDENCY (the `rusqlite` crate) and VS Code flushes that DB only every ~60 s when idle, so even a correct reader lags by up to a minute.

THE TRANSCRIPT LINES HAVE NO TIMESTAMPS AND NO MODEL. A real 2,093-line trajectory had exactly three keys per line ({type, status, payload}). The elapsed timer and the model id are only available from the hook payload, not from the transcript.

THE OFFICIAL DOCS EXPLICITLY WARN THAT THE TRANSCRIPT SCHEMA MAY CHANGE ("please build any hook consumers to be resilient"), AND THE PAYLOAD KEY IS NOT ALWAYS THE `type` VALUE (grep_search_v2 keeps the payload key `grep_search`). Deriving the payload key from `type` will silently lose events.

INSTALLING A HOOK MEANS WRITING TO THE USER'S WINDSURF CONFIG (`%USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\hooks.json`), which is a side effect outside Discodex's current read-only adapter contract, must MERGE rather than clobber (Cascade merges system+user+workspace hook files), and should be explicit opt-in.

HOOKS DO NOT RUN IN RESTRICTED MODE, and per the official exit-code table only pre-hooks (pre_user_prompt, pre_read_code, pre_write_code, pre_run_command, pre_mcp_tool_use) can block with exit 2 — post-hooks cannot, so the adapter must not rely on hook output for anything but observation.

PRIVACY LEAK RISK IN THE HOOK PATH. The hook payload contains the user prompt, the full markdown response, MCP arguments and results, and file edit diffs. The sanitizing step must run INSIDE the hook (before anything touches disk), and the Rust parser must re-sanitize; a hook that simply dumps stdin to a file would publish conversation content to a local log.

THE PRODUCT IS MID-RENAME (Windsurf -> Devin Desktop). Paths split across `~/.codeium/windsurf/...` (cascade store, hooks), `~/.windsurf/transcripts/...` (transcripts, worktrees) and `%APPDATA%\Windsurf` / `%APPDATA%\Windsurf - Next` (IDE state). A rename could move any of them, and the extension id `codeium.windsurf` may change.
THE CLI (Cascade/Windsurf CLI, `wsc`) has no session store of its own — it drives the IDE over the extension, and it is macOS-only. A CLI-only user produces no local Cascade log.
THE HOOKS-ONLY TRANSCRIPT IS WHAT OTHER TOOLS ALREADY DEPEND ON, so the 100-file / prune-oldest-by-mtime cap in the transcripts directory can delete a conversation Discodex is tailing mid-run.

MEDIUM on the read-only transcript payload VALUE shapes for tool steps (the per-type payload key names for view_file/run_command/etc. are not verified — only the type names and the {type,status,payload} envelope are). LOW-UNVERIFIED on the state.vscdb route (two upstream sources conflict on whether current builds store Cascade transcripts there). The Cascade CLI was checked for a separate session store and none was found — it is a front-end over the IDE, not an independent log producer.
summary: Windsurf/Cascade DOES have a local, machine-readable activity source, but not the one a read-only adapter would want. Three stores exist: (1) the native Cascade transcript, plaintext JSONL at %USERPROFILE%\.windsurf\transcripts\{trajectory_id}.jsonl, one file per conversation, append-only and incrementally readable — but it is only materialized once the user registers the documented `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook, and its lines carry no timestamps and no model id; (2) the always-on conversation store at %USERPROFILE%\.codeium\windsurf\cascade\{cascade_id}.pb, which is AES-256-GCM sealed (hardcoded key in the language server) and rewritten wholesale per conversation — decryptable in principle, but it needs a new `aes-gcm` dependency, a hand-rolled protobuf decoder, and a snapshot-diff reader instead of the existing line tailer, and it mirrors only the active trajectory; (3) a legacy VS Code `state.vscdb` route whose viability is contradicted between sources. The officially supported integration point is the Cascade HOOK system (12 events, JSON on stdin with agent_action_name, trajectory_id, execution_id, ISO-8601 timestamp, model_name and a tool_info object carrying file_path / command_line / cwd). A Discodex-supplied hook that appends a sanitized JSON line to a Discodex-owned file would slot straight into the EXISTING LogTailer contract and reach Codex/DSH-level richness (project, model, file basename, normalized tool activity, phase, elapsed timer). Verdict: "partial" — rich only with a one-time, opt-in hook registration; without it, the best read-only reach is project + tool activity + file basename from the transcript, with no timer and no model.
